poolReview.rationale: Explicit owner selected documented survival sequence has immediate intrinsic pull and a meaningful payoff in the precise chronology and later witness; no invented alternative-topic pool.

candidates.subject: He Survived Two Atomic Bombs
candidates.novelty: A return home after one catastrophe placed an injured survivor in the city struck three days later.
candidates.evidenceFeasibility: First-person retrospective testimony is corroborated in core chronology by independent contemporary reporting and official bombing records; recollection-level details remain attributed.
candidates.explanatoryPayoff: One injured shipbuilding engineer returned from Hiroshima to his home city, Nagasaki, before the second bombing. His official double-exposure recognition does not make him the only double survivor. His later witness serves remembrance and nuclear abolition.
candidates.visualPotential: Portrait to Hiroshima street, restrained light/aftermath, geographic journey and train, Nagasaki workplace and second light, reflective witness ending.
candidates.audienceCuriosity: How did one man come to be in both cities, and what did survival actually mean?
candidates.productionFeasibility: Original generated period reconstruction with deterministic layered animation, authored map, local af_heart; no licensed archival footage presumed.
candidates.portfolioDiversity: Owner-selected historical story judged on its own evidence; no category rotation or prior-film style copied.
candidates.comparison: One explicitly selected subject, narrowed to documented chronology and administrative recognition distinction.
limitations: Recollections are not independently observed1945 events.
Exact distance, train timetable, dialogue and later medical causation excluded.
Reconstruction is not archival footage or a verified facial likeness.
